assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened an entirely new platform in which interaction strength is tunable by a twist angle, giving correlated insulators, superconductivity and later topological flat-band phases. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the flat bands and the magic angle; the 2018 experiments realised them. Few recent discoveries combine a clear, simple theoretical idea with such broad experimental fallout, and it reorients a whole field of many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. That is a clean theory-plus-experiment split into three. Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, is not in the supplied credit, and other groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov) contributed substantially later. I propose the three credited names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups since 2018, with a large, still growing literature. The basic phenomenology is robust, though the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated. A prize about eight years after the discovery would be timely, if somewhat early on the interpretation of superconductivity.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit for the experimental side is shared with a postdoc and with other groups not in the credited list.
Sample-to-sample variability remains an issue for reproducibility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the principal non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions and mapping a lattice problem onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem. It explains the Mott transition and, combined with electronic-structure methods, is a routine tool for correlated materials. As a statistical-physicist I value the conceptual clarity of the mean-field limit and its wide use.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, and Georges and Kotliar formulated the mapping to an impurity model and developed the dynamical mean-field picture. Müller-Hartmann and Pruschke also contributed to the early work, and Metzner is not in the credited list. The supplied three-person credit is defensible but leaves Metzner's contribution open.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of use and extensive confirmation, including cold-atom benchmarks and quantitative materials predictions. The theory is mature. The impact is on method rather than a single discovery, which makes it a different kind of prize.
uncertainties: Whether a theoretical method suits the prize as well as a discovery does.
Metzner and Müller-Hartmann are omitted from the supplied credit.
Quantitative accuracy for realistic materials depends on the impurity solver and on the downfolding scheme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery that cytoplasm and nucleus are organised by liquid-like condensates formed by phase separation changed how cell biology is understood, and the active-droplet theory gives it a quantitative physical basis. It uses concepts from soft matter and non-equilibrium statistical physics, including nucleation, interfacial tension and driven chemical reactions, in a very concrete setting.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne, Hyman and Jülicher's 2009 P-granule work with Hyman and Brangwynne established liquid-like behaviour in vivo, and Jülicher supplied the physical theory. This is a plausible three-person configuration. Others, including Michael Rosen on in vitro phase separation and Rohit Pappu on sequence-level theory, contributed, and I cannot verify the whole attribution record here.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and independently confirmed, but the field is still arguing about which cellular structures are really liquid, how functional the condensates are, and the role of artefacts in overexpression experiments. It is early, but the core finding is solid.
uncertainties: Debate over the functional importance and the physical nature of some condensates.
Boundary between a physics and a biology or chemistry prize.
Attribution to in vitro and sequence-theory contributions beyond the three credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The time-reversal-invariant topological insulator, with the Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall prediction, the HgTe/CdTe prediction and observation, and the 3D materials, created a major field of topological band theory. It is conceptually deep and has fed into many other areas, despite the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation, Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall edge states, and Hasan's group observed 3D topological insulators. With a limit of three, a choice among Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan, Mele, Zhang and others is difficult and contentious. Mele and Bernevig/Zhang are partly excluded. I choose Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, with real reservations.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation, and the interpretation is stable. Practical devices are limited, but the scientific impact is clear. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Attribution is difficult because of more than three major contributors, and Shoucheng Zhang died in 2018.
The overlap with the 2016 prize and with Qi-Kun Xue's quantum anomalous Hall work.
Disagreement over whether theory or experiment should lead.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean, tunable Hubbard-type models, and the Mott-insulator transition and subsequent work on many-body dynamics gave a quantum simulator for strongly correlated matter. The conceptual connection to condensed-matter and statistical models is direct and appeals to my own field.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal for the Bose-Hubbard model in lattices, the Greiner-Bloch observation of the superfluid-Mott transition, and Esslinger's Fermi-Hubbard work are all credited. With five names and a limit of three, I think a theory-plus-experiment prize of Zoller, Bloch and a third could be justified, but Greiner and Esslinger have equally good claims, and Cirac is overlapping with trapped-ion and Rydberg candidates.
assessment.maturity: Experimental platform is highly mature and replicated worldwide, though the original goal of solving open Fermi-Hubbard problems (e.g. d-wave superconductivity) is not yet achieved. The 2001 and 2005 prizes for condensates and optical frequency combs have partly covered this field.
uncertainties: Five claimants with a limit of three.
Unclear how far the simulators have exceeded classical computation.
Cirac versus Greiner or Esslinger in the third place is a close call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model's particle content, and ATLAS and CMS are among the most remarkable experiments ever built. The 2013 prize recognised the theory, and the experimental discovery has not been honoured.
assessment.attribution: The three credited people are the conceivers and long-time leaders of ATLAS and CMS. Naming individuals from collaborations of thousands is inherently problematic, and the choice of spokespersons and detector pioneers over analysis leaders is a judgment call. The statutes allow an organisation only for the Peace Prize, so this issue is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The Higgs discovery in 2012 has been strongly confirmed, and its properties have been measured to ever greater precision. The recognition is timely, but the attribution problem is severe.
uncertainties: Fair attribution within very large collaborations.
Whether instrument builders and spokespersons are the right choice over analysts and accelerator specialists.
The scientific novelty may be seen as already recognised by the 2013 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and survey propagation applied replica-symmetry-breaking ideas from spin glasses to random satisfiability, coding and optimisation problems, revealing glassy phase transitions in computational hardness. It is close to my own research interests in disordered systems and neural networks, and its influence on information theory and machine learning is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Mézard, Parisi and Virasoro developed the cavity method for spin glasses, and Mézard and Zecchina carried it to constraint satisfaction. Parisi has already shared the 2021 prize for the origin of replica symmetry breaking, so the core originality is largely recognised. Mézard and Zecchina are a coherent pair, but the foundational credit sits partly with Parisi's group.
assessment.maturity: Developed over two decades and well tested numerically, with rigorous proofs for several cases, but the application to real computational hardness is less settled. The 2021 prize reduces the novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2021 prize to Parisi.
How far practical algorithms benefited.
Rigorous status of some predictions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance show that quantum computation is possible in principle despite noise, and topological codes link it to many-body physics. Recent below-threshold experiments make the idea tangible.
assessment.attribution: Shor's code and fault-tolerance work, Steane's independent code and Kitaev's toric code and anyon-based computation are all decisive, with Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and others also essential. A limit of three cannot cover this field fairly. I choose Shor and Kitaev, with Steane as a plausible third.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are recent and the full practical route to useful fault-tolerant machines is not yet clear, so recognition is perhaps a little early, though the theory is established.
uncertainties: Other major contributors cannot be included.
Practical impact is not established.
Overlap with recent quantum-information prizes.
